conv_148.speaker: DameTallowhelm
conv_148.text: A fief belongs to the one who keeps its wells full and its walls mended. Lordship is a duty, not a prize.

conv_148.speaker: OldTideWarden
conv_148.text: Duty is fine, but the people of {town} do not care who holds the title. They care who feeds them through the winter.

conv_148.speaker: DameTallowhelm
conv_148.text: Feeding them is worth nothing if the next raid takes {village} while {troop_count} men stand idle at the gate.

conv_148.speaker: OldTideWarden
conv_148.text: Then tell me who should hold {town} when the garrison is paid in {gold} and the ledgers are empty.

conv_148.speaker: DameTallowhelm
conv_148.text: A ledger does not defend a wall. Give {town} to a warden who knows the water, and let the fens teach the rest.

conv_148.speaker: OldTideWarden
conv_148.text: Patience wins more fens than swords do, and you know it. Let them answer for {village} before you hand over the keys.

conv_148.speaker: DameTallowhelm
conv_148.text: We will not settle this over one fief, friend. Ask me again after the spring levy and see where {town} stands.

conv_149.speaker: HammerhandVow
conv_149.text: Friends, the march on {village} begins at dawn. I need {troop_count} shields and any who will stand with me.

conv_149.speaker: DameTallowhelm
conv_149.text: Your campaigns begin with a loud speech and end with empty wells. Bring {gold} to the wells first, then talk to me.

conv_149.speaker: HammerhandVow
conv_149.text: By my hammer and my name, {village} will be defended. Those who stand with me need no speeches.

conv_149.speaker: DameTallowhelm
conv_149.text: Shields are cheap and vows are cheaper. Show me a ledger with {gold} in it, and I will listen.

conv_149.speaker: HammerhandVow
conv_149.text: My ledger is my word, and my word is worth more than any {gold} you can count.

conv_149.speaker: DameTallowhelm
conv_149.text: I will go to {town} with {troop_count} men and a full ledger. You may march alone, Hammerhand.

conv_149.speaker: HammerhandVow
conv_149.text: Then go, and see whether the wells of {town} hold when the enemy comes calling.
